newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl doubts Earth Summit deal on forest protection.
newsitem.headline: Kohl doubts Earth Summit deal on forest protection.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said in a newspaper interview to be published on Thursday he doubted the U.N. "Earth Summit" would agree to binding measures to protect forests and regulate their use.
Kohl, returning to Germany from the U.N. conference in New York, told the Rheinpfalz newspaper that he nevertheless expects the United Nations to begin preparing for a "forests conference."

"There is no more time to lose," Kohl told the newspaper published in his hometown Ludwigshafen. "If we don't rise to the challenge, the chances will increase that there will be fights in the next generation over natural resources."
Kohl said all industrial nations need to agree to binding targets for reducing greenhouse gases.
"If we can set a good example in this we will be able to credibly demand from the developing nations greater efforts to protect the global environment."

Kohl, a driving force behind a European Union initiative to cut carbon fuel emissions by 15 percent by the year 2010, said at the recent G7 summit in Denver that the gathering "was split into two blocs".
The United States, Japan and Canada did not support the EU proposal.

The environment dispute produced one of the few points of discord at the Denver summit of leading industrialised states, which meet annually to set broad economic and political policy lines for the next year.
The EU leaders from Britain, France, Germany and Italy were keen to have the final communique set a clear target for greenhouse gas reductions.
